sources.entry: chalice - A Python serverless microframework for AWS.

summary.one_liner: AWS Chalice is a Python microframework for writing and deploying serverless apps on AWS Lambda, using decorators to wire up API Gateway routes, schedules, S3, and SQS events.
summary.what_it_does: Chalice provides a command line tool (chalice new-project, chalice deploy, chalice delete) for creating, deploying, and removing a Python app on AWS. Routes and event handlers are defined with decorators such as app.route, app.schedule, app.on_s3_event, and app.on_sqs_message. The README says it integrates with Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, and other AWS services. It also states that it generates IAM policies automatically. The quickstart deploys a sample "hello world" REST API and shows the resources created (Lambda function, IAM role, Rest API).
use_cases: Build a REST API backed by AWS Lambda and API Gateway
Run periodic scheduled tasks in the cloud
Process S3 bucket upload events with a Python function
Consume messages from an SQS queue in Python
Deploy a serverless Python backend with a single command
Tear down deployed AWS resources cleanly
notable: Decorator-based API for routes, schedules, S3 events, and SQS messages
Generates IAM policies automatically during deployment
Single chalice deploy command packages and deploys the app
chalice delete removes the resources it created
caveats: Requires AWS credentials and an AWS account to deploy
Targets AWS Lambda only; the README describes no other runtime platforms
Documentation and tutorials are hosted separately from the README
